name: ComEd

summary.text: Commonwealth Edison (ComEd), a subsidiary of Exelon, is the largest electric utility in Illinois. On July 17, 2020 it entered a deferred prosecution agreement with the U.S. Attorney for the Northern District of Illinois, agreeing to pay $200 million and admitting it arranged jobs, vendor subcontracts and payments for associates of Illinois House Speaker Michael Madigan to influence legislation. Former ComEd CEO Anne Pramaggiore and three others were convicted in 2023; Madigan was convicted in February 2025.

facts.claim: ComEd agreed on July 17, 2020 to pay $200 million to resolve a federal criminal investigation into a years-long bribery scheme; prosecutors filed a single bribery count and agreed to defer prosecution for three years.
facts.quote: Commonwealth Edison Company ("ComEd"), the largest electric utility in Illinois, has agreed to pay $200 million to resolve a federal criminal investigation into a years-long bribery scheme.

sources.publisher: U.S. Attorney's Office, Northern District of Illinois
sources.title: Commonwealth Edison Agrees to Pay $200 Million to Resolve Federal Criminal Investigation

facts.claim: ComEd admitted it gave or offered jobs, vendor subcontracts and related payments for the benefit of the then-Speaker of the Illinois House and his associates in order to influence legislation affecting the company.
facts.quote: The USAO filed a single charge alleging that we improperly gave and offered to give jobs, vendor subcontracts, and payments associated with those jobs and subcontracts for the benefit of the then Speaker of the Illinois House of Representatives and the Speaker's associates.

sources.title: Exelon Corp. Form 8-K, July 2020 (ComEd deferred prosecution agreement)

facts.claim: The $200 million was payable in two $100 million installments within 30 and 90 days of filing; Exelon stated the payments would not be recovered in rates or charged to customers.
facts.quote: The payments will not be recovered in rates or charged to customers, and ComEd will not seek or accept reimbursement or indemnification from any source other than Exelon.

sources.title: Exelon Corp. Form 10-K for fiscal year 2020
Exelon Corp. Form 8-K, July 2020 (ComEd deferred prosecution agreement)

facts.claim: Former ComEd CEO Anne Pramaggiore, lobbyist Michael McClain, Jay Doherty and John Hooker were convicted in the 2023 'ComEd Four' trial of bribery conspiracy and falsifying company books; McClain and Pramaggiore were each sentenced to two years.
facts.quote: Anne Pramaggiore, Michael McClain, Jay Doherty and John Hooker were convicted of bribery conspiracy and willfully falsifying the company's books in the 2023 "ComEd Four" trial.

sources.title: Former ComEd CEO sentenced to 2 years for bribery scheme targeted at Madigan

sources.publisher: U.S. Attorney's Office, Northern District of Illinois
sources.title: Consultant Sentenced to Two Years in Federal Prison for Conspiring to Falsify Records and Evade Bribery Laws

facts.claim: Michael Madigan was convicted in February 2025 on 10 of 23 counts, the most serious tied to ComEd, and sentenced in June 2025 to 7.5 years and a $2.5 million fine.
facts.quote: The biggest convictions, including bribery, were linked to electric utility Commonwealth Edison.
